claims.text: Spray-drying produces a uniform, low-crystallinity composite precursor.
Intermediate precursor homogeneity enables synchronous thermal decomposition and reduction.
Synchronous decomposition and reduction allow noble-metal atoms to mix uniformly.
Intermediate precursor homogeneity enables formation of high-entropy alloy nanoparticles with high surface-atom exposure.
Absence of intermediate precursor homogeneity causes phase separation and segregated elemental domains.
The initial precursor contains noble metals including Pt and Ru uniformly dispersed in an amorphous or minimally crystalline matrix.
The proposed intervention is a controlled secondary heating step after spray-drying, accompanied by subtle Pt–Ru composition variation.
The comparison holds atmosphere, heating rate, metal precursors, and processing solvents constant while varying only the secondary heating profile.
The spray-dried amorphous or low-crystallinity precursor mediates subsequent nucleation and alloying during secondary heating.
A uniform precursor causes synchronous reduction and phase transformation during secondary heating.
Synchronous reduction and phase transformation make nucleation occur simultaneously throughout the material.
Simultaneous nucleation promotes homogeneous alloying and prevents phase segregation.
Optimized surface-atom mobility facilitates homogeneous alloying and is sensitive to the secondary-heating temperature profile.
Tailored secondary heating will produce HEA nanoparticles with a narrow size distribution, homogeneous elemental mixing, and a high density of catalytically active surface atoms.
The unchanged baseline will produce phase separation, elemental segregation, or uncontrolled morphologies.
The proposed mechanism applies to noble-metal-based HEA nanoparticles made by solution-mediated spray-drying followed by controlled thermal treatment.
The mechanism should not be generalized to non-noble-metal systems or methods lacking a discrete precursor-homogenization step.
The optimal secondary-heating temperature window and duration may vary with metal composition and precursor chemistry.
A lack of statistically significant structural and surface improvement over the baseline would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes subtle Pt–Ru composition variation, but the conditions state that metal precursors remain the same and only the secondary-heating profile varies.

Intermediate homogeneity created by spray-drying is identified as the causal mediator, yet both intervention and baseline batches undergo spray-drying. The comparison therefore varies secondary heating rather than the presence or degree of the proposed mediator.
